heading: INT. BELL TOWER - RUINED VILLAGE CHURCH - DAY (1944)

units.text: INT. BELL TOWER - RUINED VILLAGE CHURCH - DAY (1944)
Broken stairs.
A hole where the roof used to be.
The great bell lies on its side, cracked, big as a bathtub.
Dust drifts in a slant of light.
CORPORAL HADLEY (20s, helmet pushed back, rifle on his knee, a frayed notebook) sits on the bell's rim.
He has been here since morning.
He writes a line, crosses it out, writes another.
Below, a mile off, a flat thud of artillery rolls over the hills, and he lifts his head, listens, and returns to the notebook.
Dear Mother. It is quiet here.
units.name: HADLEY

units.text: He sighs and tears out the page.
Footsteps on the stairs.
Hadley raises the rifle.
A figure climbs through the trapdoor, hands visible, helmet askew.
NIKOLAI BRODSKY (30s, a medic with a red cross armband, a canvas bag of bandages slung across his chest) hauls himself up, coughing plaster.
Don't shoot. I'm one of yours.
units.name: NIKOLAI

units.text: Prove it.
units.name: HADLEY

units.text: I've got a bag of gauze and no sense of direction. Will that do?
units.name: NIKOLAI

units.text: Hadley lowers the rifle.
Nikolai sits on the top stair, catches his breath, takes off his helmet and rubs his scalp.
Hadley sets the notebook beside him on the bell, then shifts it to make room, then picks it up again, embarrassed.
Who sent you?
units.name: HADLEY

units.text: Nobody. My unit's gone. I followed the sound of the bell.
units.name: NIKOLAI

units.text: The bell doesn't ring. It's cracked.
units.name: HADLEY

units.text: It rang this morning. I heard it from the road.
units.name: NIKOLAI

units.text: That was me. I hit it with my boot.
units.name: HADLEY

units.text: Nikolai laughs.
Hadley almost does.
How long have you been up here?
units.name: NIKOLAI

units.text: Since dawn. I was told to watch the road.
units.name: HADLEY

units.text: And?
units.name: NIKOLAI

units.text: Nothing. A cow. A priest, I think. A cart with a woman and a goat.
units.name: HADLEY

units.text: No Germans?
units.name: NIKOLAI

units.text: Not today.
units.name: HADLEY

units.text: Nikolai opens his bag, takes out a tin of biscuits, and passes one across.
Hadley takes it, bites, chews, nods thanks.
They sit like two men on a porch, with the war rumbling a long way off.
What were you writing?
units.name: NIKOLAI

units.text: A letter.
units.name: HADLEY

units.text: To whom?
units.name: NIKOLAI

units.text: My mother. I'm not very good at it.
units.name: HADLEY

units.text: What do you say?
units.name: NIKOLAI

units.text: That it's quiet.
units.name: HADLEY

units.text: Is it?
units.name: NIKOLAI

units.text: Hadley glances at the hole in the roof, the gray sky, a bird crossing it.
Right now.
units.name: HADLEY

units.text: Nikolai finishes his biscuit.
He brushes crumbs from his knees, stands, and goes to the cracked bell, running a palm along its lip.
He picks up a small stone from the floor.
May I?
units.name: NIKOLAI

units.text: Go ahead.
units.name: HADLEY

units.text: Nikolai taps the bell with the stone.
A low, flat, broken note rolls out across the valley and dies.
Both of them wait to see if anyone answers.
No one does.
